summary: R4 retrieved the expected D1 values at three addresses with independent calibration controls. M1 additionally demonstrated that D1[D9] follows compression writes 08 -> 00 -> 08.
M1 did not reset the measured B2 drive settings during a compression toggle with a completed frame in each phase. No B2 data writes occurred in the measurement interval.
M2 did not reset those settings during direct HS display-off/display-on, before or after a completed frame. The driver wake helper was bypassed and no B2 data writes occurred in this interval.
M3 reproduced unexpected pre-fixup link and drive values on two boots with fixup disabled. The explicit manual fixup changed them to the intended values on the first boot.

The findings localize an initialization/retention problem before the fixup, but do not establish whether early writes are ignored, overwritten later, or reflected differently before internal state is ready. No physical display outcome was observed.

method_controls.visual_baseline: Not verified: the user is away. M1/M2 used a register-correct baseline and unchanged text-console pixel data, not a visually confirmed bright recovery image.
method_controls.quiescent_reads: Held tty1 in KD_GRAPHICS; paused/resumed the existing screen daemon for R4/M1/M2. All read snapshots had zero frame kickoffs. Traced both pingpong completion paths for every deliberate frame.
method_controls.isolated_M1: Sent only B1 compression and dual-link data writes between baseline and post-toggle snapshots; omitted gamma and the final normal-conditions fixup step.
method_controls.isolated_M2: Used raw HS 28/29 commands separated by 100 ms, rather than bl_power, because the installed backlight wake handler reapplies normal conditions.
method_controls.no_op_frames: Rewrote the same first four framebuffer bytes to request a frame without changing image content; verified completion on both pingpong blocks before reads.
method_controls.transport_trace: M1/M2 and the first M3 run include kprobes of msm:dsi_host_transfer capturing type, flags, length and first two payload bytes, plus transfer return values.

R4.control: Before each D1 read, alternate known D8 calibration at 5a (33) and 5b (51).
R4.limits: Expected constants alone do not prove every D1 address is a live B1 mirror. The controlled D9 changes in M1 add direct evidence for that address.

sequence: Confirm intended D1/D2 values while the display is off.
Send raw HS display-on and complete one unchanged-content frame. Confirm register baseline.
Write B1[D9]=00, complete one frame and wait one second; read registers.
Write B1[D9]=08 and B1[51]=06, complete one frame and wait one second; read registers.
M1.conclusion: The proposed compression toggle did not erase these already-correct drive-register values in this state.
limits: Does not exclude first-initialization behavior or an unmeasured internal latch changing.
No bright-image load or optical validation; no conclusion that the picture remained correct.

sequence: Establish an independent normal-conditions baseline, complete one unchanged-content frame and record registers.
Send raw HS display off (28), wait 100 ms, then raw HS display on (29).
Read before sending another frame, then complete one frame, wait one second and read again.
M2.conclusion: Off/on did not erase the measured register settings. Loss of these values was not reproduced as a wake-failure mechanism.
limits: Does not establish a successful visible wake; the raw-command test bypasses UI behavior.
Does not test the previously troublesome large bright image or prove the panel power/output stage stayed healthy.

M3.configuration_reason: Prevent automatic fixup and screen-daemon wake writes from overwriting the state being measured. The panel is a module loaded after the installed root starts, so no image modification was needed.
boot_checks: Screen daemon was masked and inactive.
No automatic fixup-step messages occurred before the measurements.
Display had reached its normal post-boot state with bl_power=0; the image was not observed.

first_boot_manual_fixup.note: This count includes a gamma update-key write plus the five normal-condition B2 data writes. The manual fixup does more than change compression.

M3.second_boot_control: Rebooted with the same diagnostic option, without running the fixup. Read every D1/D2 location twice with D8=33 and D8=51 controls interleaved; all unexpected values reproduced exactly.
M3.conclusion: The intended post-initialization register values are not present before the fixup on this build. The manual fixup supplies them; the result cannot be explained solely as all the intended readable values already being present before it.
limits: Measurements are after boot and initial frame activity, not immediately after each initialization command. They cannot distinguish initial write rejection from later reset/overwrite.
The meaning of D1[D9]=e5 in this state is not established; it is a reproducible measured byte, not a claimed reset default.
The manual fixup applies gamma/update and normal drive writes as well as compression changes, so its success does not isolate the corrective operation.
The readback bank may not expose every internal output/latch state. No visible garbling, colour correction or wake success was confirmed.

M3.note: The manual fixup includes gamma/update and normal-condition writes; it is not a compression-only test.

recommended_next_evidence: Capture the ordering of reset release, TCON-ready, clock-lane transitions, initialization sends and first frame. These tests did not measure clock state during reset.
Locate the first stage where intended D1/D2 values are absent using carefully controlled pre-frame checkpoints, accounting for reads themselves potentially changing panel state.
Do not base the redesign on compression or display off/on always erasing B2 settings; that mechanism was not observed in the controlled steady-state tests.
Retain physical colour, dimming and wake checks when the user returns; register agreement alone cannot qualify display behavior.
